description: Login throttle: a package-level map is read and written by concurrent gin handlers with no lock, so concurrent logins hit Go's fatal 'concurrent map writes' and crash the server.
notes: FM-07 (concurrency and shared state). failedLogins is a plain package-level map read by loginThrottled and written by recordFailedLogin/resetFailedLogins/pruneFailedLogins from concurrent gin handler goroutines with no mutex. Concurrent logins trigger Go's unrecoverable `fatal error: concurrent map writes` (or map read and map write), which kills the whole server, and attempts.count is a data race. It's also per-process, so it doesn't hold across instances. Severity important: FM-07 is important unless it double-grants money or goods; it needs concurrent logins (normal load). Reading severity accuracy: critical is defensible here. Any client can trigger the crash with a few concurrent failed logins, and Argus's critical row includes a broken production system, so a critical grade still scores as a true positive but not as severity-correct; read a critical on this task as a calibration difference, not a miss. Fix: guard the map with a sync.Mutex (or use a shared store). The 429 wiring and the single-threaded test are legitimate.
